topic: Pleiotropy (PKU, Pea Starch) & Polygenic Skin Color (1:6:15:20:15:6:1)
quickSummary: Pleiotropy: single gene influences multiple phenotypic traits (Phenylketonuria PKU, Starch grain size vs seed shape in peas). summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Pleiotropy occurs when one single gene influences multiple, distinct phenotypic traits (e.g. PKU enzyme mutation causing mental retardation and hypopigmentation; Pea starch Bb gene). Polygenic inheritance occurs when multiple additive gene pairs control a single continuous trait (e.g. Human skin color A, B, C genes yielding a 1:6:15:20:15:6:1 Gaussian distribution across 64 combinations).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PLEIOTROPY vs POLYGENIC INHERITANCE
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
   PLEIOTROPY                                              POLYGENIC INHERITANCE
   ONE single gene influences MULTIPLE,                    MULTIPLE additive genes control
   apparently unrelated phenotypic traits.                 a SINGLE continuous trait.
   ├── Phenylketonuria (PKU)                               ├── Human Skin Color (A, B, C genes)
   └── Starch grain size vs seed shape in Peas             └── Wheat Kernel Color (1:4:6:4:1)
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 5.1 Pleiotropy: Single Gene, Multiple Phenotypes
1. **Phenylketonuria (PKU)**: Mutation in a single autosomal gene encoding **Phenylalanine Hydroxylase (PAH)** prevents conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine. Clinical pleiotropic symptoms: mental retardation, microcephaly, hair hypopigmentation, and skin eczema.
2. **Starch Synthesis in Garden Peas (*B* Gene)**:
   - $BB \longrightarrow$ Large starch grains $\rightarrow$ Round seeds.
   - $bb \longrightarrow$ Small starch grains $\rightarrow$ Wrinkled seeds.
   - $Bb \longrightarrow$ Intermediate starch grain size (*Incomplete dominance for size*), but Round seeds (*Complete dominance for shape*).
   - *Conclusion*: Dominance is not an autonomous intrinsic property of a gene, but depends on the specific phenotypic product being assayed!

### 5.2 Polygenic (Quantitative) Inheritance

```
                      POLYGENIC PHENOTYPIC DISTRIBUTION
                      
   Dominant Alleles:     0     1     2     3     4     5     6
   F2 Ratio:             1  :  6  : 15  : 20  : 15  :  6  :  1  (Total = 64)
```

- **Human Skin Color (Davenport Additive Model)**: Controlled by 3 additive gene pairs ($A, B, C$).
  - $AABBCC \longrightarrow$ Very Dark / Black ($6$ dominant alleles).
  - $aabbcc \longrightarrow$ Very Light / White ($0$ dominant alleles).
  - $AaBbCc \longrightarrow$ Intermediate / Mulatto ($3$ dominant alleles).
  - $F_2$ cross of mulattoes ($AaBbCc \times AaBbCc$) yields $64$ combinations with $7$ phenotypic classes: **$1:6:15:20:15:6:1$**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Wheat Kernel Color (Nilsson-Ehle Model)
conceptBreakdown.title: Wheat Kernel Color (Nilsson-Ehle Model)
conceptBreakdown.content: Wheat kernel redness is governed by two polygenic loci (R1, R2); cross of dark red (R1R1R2R2) and white (r1r1r2r2) yields a 1:4:6:4:1 phenotypic ratio across 16 combinations.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Continuous Gaussian Bell-Curve Variation
conceptBreakdown.title: Continuous Gaussian Bell-Curve Variation
conceptBreakdown.content: Polygenic traits (human height, intelligence, skin color) generate continuous normal distribution curves with intermediate phenotypes being the most abundant and extreme phenotypes rare.
